name: Puck Fair

attributes.attribute: held in Kilorgin near the feast of Lughnasa
captured and crowned king for the fair
taken to the mountains and released at the end

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Puck Fair is an Irish folk festival that closes in on the old Celtic harvest feast of Lughnasa. It takes place in the small town of Kilorglin, in the province of Munster. A wild goat is caught in the nearby mountains and crowned king in the square. Hoisted aloft, the goat rules over three days. The three days are named for gathering, for the fair, and for scattering. The events span horse shows, games, music, and drink. At the end the goat is returned to the mountains and set free. Locals say the feast is old, but some view it as a recent custom, perhaps 300 years old. The goat and the British word puck support that newer claim.

okr.objective: Describe Puck Fair and the crowning and release of the wild goat in Kilorgin.
